name: CrewAI Hierarchical Process (manager-delegated crew)
aliases: Process.hierarchical; manager_llm crew; crew manager
short_description: A CrewAI crew where an auto-created or custom manager agent plans, delegates tasks to role-defined agents (role/goal/backstory) and validates outcomes.
topology: Star: manager over role agents; manager uses delegation tools.
communication_pattern: Manager issues delegate/ask-coworker tool calls; agents return task outputs.
coordination_mechanism: Manager allocates tasks by capability, reviews outputs, decides completion; optional planning step.
typical_roles: Manager (no tools); Role agents e.g. Researcher, Analyst, Writer
memory_model: Crew memory (short-term, long-term, entity) optional; task outputs passed as context.
characteristics: Role/goal/backstory persona prompts; Manager should not have tools; Default is sequential, hierarchical opt-in
strengths: Very fast to prototype; Readable role definitions; Built-in validation step
weaknesses: Manager delegation can be unpredictable; Less fine-grained control than graph frameworks
failure_modes: Manager over-delegates or loops on validation; Persona prompts drift from tasks
cost_latency_profile: Medium-high; manager reasoning on every delegation.
best_use_cases: Research-and-report crews; Content generation from scraped data
research_scraping_fit: Convenient for small research crews; for bulk scraping prefer deterministic flows.
variants: manager_llm auto manager; custom manager_agent; planning=True

name: Evolving / Learned Orchestrator (Puppeteer)
aliases: puppeteer-puppets; RL-trained orchestrator; dynamic sequencing
short_description: A centralized orchestrator ("puppeteer") trained with reinforcement learning dynamically sequences which agent ("puppet") acts next, learning compact, often cyclic, efficient orchestration over time.
topology: Star with learned sequencing; emergent compact/cyclic subgraphs.
communication_pattern: Orchestrator activates one agent at a time with evolving state.
coordination_mechanism: RL policy optimising quality and cost.
typical_roles: Puppeteer policy; Puppet agents (reasoning styles, tools)
strengths: Prunes useless agents; Adapts to task distribution
failure_modes: Reward hacking; Poor transfer to new task types
scalability: Policy scales to many candidate agents.
best_use_cases: Mature production swarms with logged tasks and measurable quality
research_scraping_fit: Later-stage optimisation once you have evals for your research swarm.

name: Hierarchical Teams (supervisor of supervisors)
aliases: multi-level hierarchy; tree of managers; nested teams; hierarchical swarm
short_description: Generalises the supervisor pattern into a tree: a top-level manager delegates to team leads, each of which supervises its own workers.
topology: Tree (2+ levels). Communication follows parent-child edges only.
communication_pattern: Top-down task assignment, bottom-up reporting; teams are subgraphs.
coordination_mechanism: Recursive decomposition; each mid-level supervisor owns a sub-goal and returns a summary.
typical_roles: Top-level director; Team supervisors (e.g. research team, writing team); Leaf workers
memory_model: Scoped state per team (subgraph state / checkpoint namespace); summaries pass upward.
characteristics: Information hiding between teams; Span-of-control limits per manager; Composable subgraphs
strengths: Scales beyond single-supervisor limits; Teams reusable as modules; Parallel teams
weaknesses: More hops = more latency and information loss; Harder to debug across levels; Over-engineering for small tasks
failure_modes: Telephone-game distortion across levels; Mid-level managers duplicate each other; Budget blow-up from deep recursion
scalability: High: number of agents grows with branching factor^depth.
cost_latency_profile: High tokens; latency grows with depth but parallel subtrees help.
best_use_cases: Large research projects split into topic teams (search team, scrape team, analysis team, writing team); Enterprise workflows mirroring org charts
research_scraping_fit: Good when a crawl has distinct domains (e.g. per-site scraping teams under a research director).
variants: LangGraph hierarchical agent teams; CrewAI hierarchical process; TalkHier; Swarms HierarchicalSwarm; Nested agents-as-tools
example_frameworks_or_implementations: LangGraph Hierarchical Agent Teams; langgraph-supervisor multi-level; CrewAI Process.hierarchical; Google ADK hierarchical task decomposition

aliases: LLM as controller; tool/model orchestration; JARVIS
short_description: An LLM controller performs task planning, selects expert models (from a model hub) per subtask, executes them and generates the response.
topology: Star: controller LLM over many specialised non-LLM or LLM experts.
communication_pattern: Structured task specs (JSON) to experts; results back to controller.
coordination_mechanism: Four stages: planning, model selection (by description), execution, response generation.
memory_model: Task list with dependencies and resource references.

strengths: Leverages specialised models cheaply; Modular
weaknesses: Dependent on quality of model descriptions; Planning errors
failure_modes: Wrong expert chosen; Format mismatches between experts
scalability: Large expert pools possible with retrieval over descriptions.
cost_latency_profile: Moderate; expert calls can be cheap.
best_use_cases: Pipelines mixing OCR, vision, NER, translation on scraped content
research_scraping_fit: Useful when scraped data needs specialised processors (PDF OCR, image captioning, NER).

name: LLMCompiler (parallel task DAG)
aliases: task DAG planner; parallel function calling
short_description: A planner emits a DAG of tool/agent tasks with dependencies; a task-fetching unit dispatches ready tasks in parallel; a joiner decides to answer or replan.
topology: DAG of tasks generated at runtime; planner -> scheduler -> parallel executors -> joiner.
coordination_mechanism: Dependency graph scheduling (like a compiler).
typical_roles: Planner; Task fetching unit / scheduler; Executors; Joiner
memory_model: Task results keyed by task id.
characteristics: Max parallelism given dependencies; Streaming planning
strengths: Lower latency and cost than sequential ReAct; Good for many independent lookups
failure_modes: Missing dependency -> task runs with empty input; Over-parallelism hits rate limits
best_use_cases: Fetching many pages/entities in parallel then combining; Multi-source fact gathering
research_scraping_fit: Very good for scraping many URLs with partial dependencies (list page -> N detail pages).
poor_fit_use_cases: Tasks with long chains of strict dependencies

name: Magentic-One (Orchestrator with task & progress ledgers)
aliases: Magentic orchestration; ledger-based orchestrator
short_description: A generalist orchestrator keeps an outer-loop Task Ledger (facts, guesses, plan) and inner-loop Progress Ledger, directing WebSurfer, FileSurfer, Coder and ComputerTerminal agents and replanning when stuck.
topology: Star around Orchestrator; specialists include a browser agent.
communication_pattern: Orchestrator selects next agent and instruction each step; agents reply.
coordination_mechanism: Two nested loops: task ledger planning and progress ledger self-reflection (is task done? are we looping? who next?).
characteristics: Stall detection and replanning; Modular agents plug in/out
strengths: Robust to dead ends via stall counter; Strong on web tasks (GAIA, WebArena)
weaknesses: Many LLM calls; slow; Browser agents are brittle
failure_modes: Loops between agents; Risky web actions without human approval
scalability: Small fixed team; replicate for throughput.
cost_latency_profile: High cost and latency per task.
best_use_cases: Complex web navigation and research requiring browsing, downloading, coding
research_scraping_fit: Excellent template for agentic browsing/scraping tasks requiring interaction (forms, pagination, JS sites).
poor_fit_use_cases: Bulk static scraping (use crawlers); Cost-sensitive workloads
variants: Magentic-One; Semantic Kernel Magentic orchestration; MagenticOneGroupChat

name: Orchestrator-Worker (Lead agent + subagents)
aliases: orchestrator-workers; lead agent / subagents; manager-worker; agents-as-tools; subagents pattern
short_description: A central LLM decomposes a task at runtime, spawns or calls specialised worker agents (often in parallel, each with its own context window) and synthesises their condensed results.
topology: Star: one orchestrator hub, N worker spokes; workers do not talk to each other.
communication_pattern: Request/response between hub and spokes (tool calls or spawned sub-runs); workers return condensed summaries.
coordination_mechanism: Dynamic task decomposition by the orchestrator; explicit task briefs (objective, output format, tools, boundaries); orchestrator decides when to stop.
typical_roles: Orchestrator/lead; Worker/subagent (searcher, analyst, coder); Optional synthesiser or citation agent
memory_model: Orchestrator holds global plan (often persisted to external memory); each worker has an isolated, short-lived context; only distilled results flow back.
characteristics: Subtasks not known in advance; Context isolation per worker; Parallelism at the worker level; Single owner of final answer
strengths: Breadth-first exploration in parallel; Keeps orchestrator context clean; Easy to reason about and trace; Effort can scale with query complexity
weaknesses: Orchestrator is a bottleneck and single point of failure; High token usage (Anthropic reports ~15x a chat for multi-agent); Workers cannot coordinate directly, so duplicated work is possible
failure_modes: Vague delegation causes overlapping or off-scope subagents; Spawning too many subagents for simple queries; Lossy summaries drop key evidence; Orchestrator stops too early or loops forever
scalability: Good to ~10-20 parallel workers per orchestrator; beyond that, add hierarchy.
cost_latency_profile: High tokens, low wall-clock when workers run in parallel; latency bounded by slowest worker plus synthesis.
best_use_cases: Open-ended web research and deep research reports; Parallel scraping of many sites/sources with a central aggregator; Coding tasks touching many files
research_scraping_fit: Excellent default for research swarms: lead agent plans, subagents each search/scrape a slice, lead synthesises and a citation pass attributes claims.
poor_fit_use_cases: Tasks needing tight shared context between all agents; Simple fixed pipelines (use prompt chaining); Low-budget, latency-insensitive single lookups
variants: Agents-as-tools (manager keeps ownership); Spawned subagents with separate context windows; Lead + CitationAgent post-pass; Dynamic effort scaling (1 agent for facts, 10+ for complex research)
example_frameworks_or_implementations: Anthropic Claude Research; Claude Code subagents; OpenAI Agents SDK Agent.as_tool(); LangChain subagents pattern; Strands agents-as-tools; smolagents managed agents

name: Plan-and-Execute
aliases: planner-executor; plan-and-solve agent; planner/replanner
short_description: A planner LLM writes a multi-step plan up front; executor agent(s) carry out steps with tools; a replanner revises the plan from results.
topology: Pipeline with feedback: Planner -> Executor(s) -> Replanner -> (Executor | Finish).
communication_pattern: Plan object passed down; step results passed back to replanner.
coordination_mechanism: Explicit plan as shared artifact; replanning loop.
memory_model: Plan + past steps list in shared state.
characteristics: Separates long-horizon reasoning from tool execution; Executor can be a smaller model
strengths: Fewer calls to the expensive model; Forces explicit thinking about the whole task; Plan is auditable
weaknesses: Static plans go stale when web results surprise; Sequential by default
failure_modes: Plan too coarse or hallucinated steps; Replanner rubber-stamps failures
scalability: Single-thread unless steps are parallelised (see LLMCompiler).
cost_latency_profile: Lower cost than ReAct on long tasks; latency still sequential.
best_use_cases: Multi-step research questions with predictable structure; Scrape jobs with known site sequence (login -> list -> detail pages)
research_scraping_fit: Good for structured scraping jobs and literature reviews with known phases.
poor_fit_use_cases: Highly exploratory tasks where the next step depends heavily on surprises
variants: Plan-and-Solve prompting; ReWOO; LLMCompiler; BabyAGI task list
key_sources: LangChain blog: Plan-and-Execute agents (Plan-and-execute, ReWOO, LLMCompiler) <https://blog.langchain.dev/planning-agents/>; Lei Wang et al. (2023) Plan-and-Solve Prompting: Improving Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought Reasoning by Large Language Models <https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.04091>

name: ReWOO (Reasoning WithOut Observation)
aliases: planner-worker-solver; decoupled reasoning
short_description: Planner writes the full plan with evidence placeholders (#E1, #E2) up front; workers execute tools filling placeholders; a solver composes the answer. No LLM call between tool steps.
topology: Three-stage pipeline: Planner -> Worker(s) -> Solver.
communication_pattern: Variable substitution of tool outputs into plan.
coordination_mechanism: Pre-declared dependency variables.
strengths: Large token savings vs ReAct; Workers can run tools without LLM
weaknesses: Cannot adapt mid-way to observations; Planner errors propagate
failure_modes: Placeholder chain breaks when a tool returns unexpected format
scalability: Good; tool calls can be parallel if independent.
best_use_cases: Predictable lookup chains (search X, fetch page, extract Y); Cheap high-volume enrichment
research_scraping_fit: Strong for cheap, repetitive enrichment scrapes where the steps are known.
poor_fit_use_cases: Exploratory browsing; Sites requiring adaptive navigation
key_sources: Binfeng Xu et al. (2023) ReWOO: Decoupling Reasoning from Observations for Efficient Augmented Language Models <https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18323>; LangChain blog: Plan-and-Execute agents (Plan-and-execute, ReWOO, LLMCompiler) <https://blog.langchain.dev/planning-agents/>

name: Supervisor (LLM-routed worker graph)
aliases: supervisor architecture; agent supervisor; group manager
short_description: A supervisor LLM node repeatedly picks which specialist agent acts next (or FINISH), receiving each agent's output back before choosing again.
topology: Star with a loop: supervisor <-> each worker; workers return to supervisor after each step.
communication_pattern: Turn-based routing; handoff tools or Command routing; shared or partially shared message history.
coordination_mechanism: Supervisor selects next worker from descriptions + state; can call several in parallel or map-reduce.
memory_model: Shared graph state (message list) usually visible to supervisor; output_mode controls whether full worker history or last message is added.
characteristics: Sequential multi-step loop; Explicit FINISH decision; Workers can be whole sub-agents
strengths: Simple mental model; Easy to add/remove specialists; Natural checkpointing in graph frameworks
weaknesses: Extra LLM call per routing step; Supervisor context grows with worker outputs; Translation loss when supervisor paraphrases worker results
failure_modes: Ping-pong between two workers; Supervisor never emits FINISH; Wrong specialist chosen due to vague descriptions
scalability: Moderate: routing accuracy degrades as worker count grows (tool selection overload); nest into hierarchy for >~10 workers.
cost_latency_profile: Medium-high; one supervisor call per hop adds latency.
best_use_cases: Research assistant with search, scrape, analysis and writing specialists; Mixed tool domains needing different prompts
research_scraping_fit: Good for interactive research where next step depends on last result (search -> scrape -> analyse -> search again).
poor_fit_use_cases: Embarrassingly parallel bulk scraping (fan-out is cheaper); Hard real-time
variants: Tool-calling supervisor (workers as tools); Command-based routing in LangGraph; Parallel tool-call supervisor
example_frameworks_or_implementations: LangGraph supervisor / langgraph-supervisor; CrewAI hierarchical manager; Swarms HierarchicalSwarm

name: Task-Queue Agent Loop (BabyAGI-style)
aliases: task creation / prioritization / execution loop; autonomous task list; job-queue agents
short_description: Three cooperating roles run in a loop over a shared task list: an execution agent completes the top task, a creation agent adds new tasks from results, a prioritisation agent reorders the queue.
topology: Ring/loop around a shared task queue and vector memory.
communication_pattern: Agents read/write a shared queue and results store.
coordination_mechanism: Priority queue + objective; memory retrieval for context.
typical_roles: Execution agent; Task creation agent; Prioritisation agent
memory_model: Vector store of task results + task queue.
strengths: Simple and generalisable; Naturally extends to worker pools pulling from a queue
weaknesses: Unbounded task growth; Drifts from objective
failure_modes: Infinite task generation; Duplicate tasks; Goal drift
scalability: Queue can feed many parallel workers (worker pool); needs dedup.
best_use_cases: Crawl frontier management; Long-running background research with budget caps
research_scraping_fit: The queue+workers idea maps directly onto a crawl frontier; add dedup, budgets and stop criteria.
poor_fit_use_cases: Tasks needing guaranteed termination without guardrails
variants: BabyAGI; AutoGPT-style loops; Worker pool with work stealing

coordination_mechanism: Progressive generation then cross-page synthesis/validation.
characteristics: Generate code once, run cheaply many times

best_use_cases: Repeated extraction from same-template sites
research_scraping_fit: Top pattern for scraping cost-efficiency: agents write scrapers rather than reading every page.

coordination_mechanism: Priority queues, per-host back-off, dedup tests.
strengths: Proven at web scale; Predictable
cost_latency_profile: Cheap per page (non-LLM); LLM steps add cost.
best_use_cases: Any large-scale scraping
research_scraping_fit: The right skeleton for scraping swarms: keep crawling deterministic; use LLM agents only for prioritisation, extraction and QA.

best_use_cases: Answering questions requiring deep navigation of official sites

name: Handoff Swarm (OpenAI Swarm / Agents SDK handoffs)
aliases: handoffs; transfer_to_agent; triage + specialists; agent swarm (OpenAI sense)
short_description: Agents hold the conversation one at a time and transfer control to another agent via a special handoff tool call; the receiving agent becomes active with the shared (optionally filtered) history.
topology: Directed graph of allowed handoffs (often triage hub + specialists, but any agent may hand off to any permitted agent).
communication_pattern: Single active agent; shared message context; HandoffMessage transfers.
coordination_mechanism: Handoff tools with descriptions; input filters; termination conditions.
memory_model: Shared conversation history (can be filtered/nested on handoff).
characteristics: No central orchestrator; Ownership of reply moves with control; Lightweight
strengths: Simple; minimal overhead; Focused prompts per specialist; Natural human-in-loop handoff
weaknesses: No parallelism by default; Global planning is weak; Hard to guarantee termination
failure_modes: Handoff loops (A->B->A); Context bloat as history passes along; Specialist lacks info lost in filtering
scalability: Moderate; handoff graph complexity grows quickly.
cost_latency_profile: Low-medium; one agent active at a time.
best_use_cases: Customer-support-like routing; Interactive research assistant where specialists take over
research_scraping_fit: Fine for interactive assistants; weak for large parallel scraping.
poor_fit_use_cases: Bulk parallel work; Tasks needing synthesis across specialists (use agents-as-tools)

name: Model / LLM Routing (cost-quality router)
aliases: RouteLLM; LLM cascade; MasRouter
short_description: A learned router assigns each query (or each agent role in a MAS) to the cheapest model likely to succeed, escalating to stronger models when needed.

coordination_mechanism: Learned preference/quality predictor; thresholds.
strengths: Large cost savings at similar quality
failure_modes: Under-routing hard queries to weak models
best_use_cases: High-volume extraction where most pages are easy; Assigning cheap models to worker roles, strong to lead
research_scraping_fit: Very valuable for scraping swarms: cheap models for extraction, strong models for planning/synthesis.

best_use_cases: Routing URLs to site-specific scrapers/parsers; Routing queries to search vs DB vs calculator

name: Stigmergy (indirect coordination via environment)
